title: Discovering Power
coreMove: Look beneath the obvious contest for the hidden asymmetry that changes what strength means.
sourcePressure: David and Goliath, Wal-Mart, and Marshall and Roche point to hidden power: change the terms of contest, find the reinforcing system, or impose asymmetric costs instead of matching the visible fight.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Power means being bigger, louder, better funded, or more determined.

sourceAnchors.name: David and Goliath
sourceAnchors.detail: the chapter-map snippets list David and Goliath as a basic strategy story where the contest changes when one side refuses the opponent's preferred terms
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: David wins strategic power by refusing to play the giant's game on the giant's terms.

sourceAnchors.name: Wal-Mart network
sourceAnchors.detail: secondary support says Wal-Mart's advantage came from the network rather than isolated visible store practices
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Wal-Mart's secret was not a store trick to copy; the power sat in the reinforcing network behind the store.

sourceAnchors.name: Marshall and Roche strategy against the Soviet Union
sourceAnchors.detail: chapter-map support names Marshall and Roche using U.S. technological strengths to impose higher Soviet response costs instead of matching weapon systems directly
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Marshall and Roche looked for the response that made the other side pay more to keep up.
